# Oncobase

> Oncobase is an open-source (MIT) knowledge base for taking control of your care. Publish a vault of markdown notes, papers, and results to a searchable reader with AI search and chat, role-based privacy, inline redaction, and clinical viewers.

It was inspired by Sid Sijbrandij's osteosarc.com (https://osteosarc.com/).

## Start here

- [Oncobase](https://oncobase.io/): what it is and who it is for.
- [Everything Oncobase can do](https://oncobase.io/features.md): every feature, where it lives, and how to call it, in markdown. The same content as the [features page](https://oncobase.io/features).
- [How Oncobase compares](https://oncobase.io/compare.md): when to use Notion, Obsidian, Yuga Bio, and others instead, and what to reuse if you are building your own. The same content as the [comparison page](https://oncobase.io/compare).
- [Source code and README](https://github.com/jasonLaster/oncobase): MIT licensed.
- [Diana's knowledge base](https://diana-tnbc.com/): the first site built on Oncobase.

## Two ways to use it with an agent

- Have your agent build your own knowledge base with the `oncobase` CLI (`oncobase check`, then `oncobase publish`) and the bundled skills (`oncobase skills`).
- Or have your agent reference Oncobase while it builds yours: the code is MIT licensed, so any part can be read, copied, and adapted.

## Notes for agents

- The reader is a client-rendered web app; most content needs a signed-in session or the site password.
- The public guides at https://diana-tnbc.com/education need no password, and neither do this site's pages (the home page, features, and compare).
